lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.quote: An unrelated lawful ground for detention must be examined separately.
lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.note: A complete traps section is now present after the worked examples.

lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.quote: A **quasi-judicial body** is an agency outside the courts that hears facts and decides certain disputes.
lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.note: All five formerly undefined terms now receive plain explanations.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: This does not excuse a separate crime.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Sole-belief detention is explained and applied with its separate-crime limitation.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: An accusation alone is not a conviction.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Forced service and the due-conviction punishment exception are explained and applied.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Section $19$ forbids excessive fines and cruel, degrading, or inhuman punishment.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Excessive fines are applied and the other Section 19 protections and current statutory penalty rules are taught.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: A lawful conviction does not give officials permission to abuse a prisoner.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Punishment protections include degrading treatment, prison conditions, and current death-penalty replacement rules.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Conviction or acquittal under either bars another prosecution under the other for the same act.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Same-offense conditions and the distinct law/ordinance same-act rule are taught.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: An **ex post facto law** applies a harmful criminal-law change backward.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The meaning and applications to earlier lawful conduct and increased punishment are given.
The definition and an identified-group example show punishment without judicial trial.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Use available evidence, such as records, witness accounts, or medical findings.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The lesson teaches evidence-based fact checking, rule matching, and a worked abuse analysis.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: The missed work harms the family's income and ability to meet daily needs.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The family example traces stated detention facts to lost income and daily-needs effects.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: A lawyer can assess a petition for a writ of habeas corpus.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Legal help, court review of detention, and CHR investigation and assistance are distinguished.

lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.quote: Filing a complaint alone does not meet these conditions.
lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.note: Double jeopardy now has a definition, attachment conditions, applications, and exceptions.
